description: Use this when the user wants to start tracking time on a project. Takes the project by its name (`project`) or by its ID (`projectId`), so it needs no project_list or timer_status call first: if the name matches no project or several, or a timer is already running, nothing is started and the result says why. The timer starts now unless `startDateTime` gives an earlier time.

description.description: What the work is, such as "Answering tickets", when the request says so next to the project. Saved as the description of the entry. Never the name of the timer or the project. Leave it out when it is not known.

project.description: The project's name as the request gives it, such as "Website redesign". A timer or an entry is named after its project: in a request for "the Acme timer", the project is "Acme". Upper and lower case, spaces and hyphens don't have to match. Leave it out when the request names no project. Use this or projectId.

projectId.description: The project's ID, when an earlier result already gave it. Use this or project.

startDateTime.description: Optional start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2025-10-08T10:30:00Z"). If not provided, uses current time.

name: timer_start

duration.description: Duration of the running task in seconds

pause.description: The current break, while the timer is paused

task.description: The running task, with its project. Absent when no timer runs.

title: Start Timer
